title: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"
description: In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me. Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides. title: Meet The Bike-Riding, Mail-Delivering Raccoon Who Dares To Challenge GTA 6
description: This November doesn't look like other Novembers, not on the game release calendar anyway. Typically, this month is reserved for the release of a few of the biggest games of the year, strategically timed to drop just before the holiday season and events like The Game Awards. But in 2026, nearly every big publisher and even lots of smaller ones backed away from November for one obvious reason: Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar's long-awaited sequel will likely break every entertainment sales record that exists. Launching in that kind of blast radius isn't an enticing prospect for most. But it didn't scare off Denkiworks, creators of Tanuki: Pon's Summer, and I wanted to know why. Speaking with him via email, game director Liam Edwards told me that while GTA 6 was certainly a consideration, there's no sense in waiting for all the stars to align because that's not what the stars do in the games industry. "Honestly, it was in everyone's mind, I think, all year. 'When is that game releasing,'" Edwards told me. "But I think for us actually, when we finally decided on November, it was a mix of: 'Okay, we have to ship and can't keep waiting around. If we delay, there are also hundreds of games like ours, other indies who will have delayed, and then we're fighting against them for attention.' There's sadly no 'right answer.'" He said that his developer friends have questioned the decision, too, but added that Denkiworks hopes Tanuki: Pon's Summer is "enough of a good time" that players will find it after playing games like GTA 6 and The Ocarina of Time remake, even if they don't catch it in this small window between that pair of November titans. I've been playing and loving Tanuki for about a week now. It's a third-person adventure game that blends elements of BMX tricks with mail delivery in a quaint Japan-inspired town, and stars a lovable raccoon trying his best--provided he gets out of bed on time. It feels like a Nintendo game that somehow went multiplatform. Characters are…

title: Queen’s Domain Has The Most Terrifying Mimic Design I’ve Ever Seen
description: I thought I was holding my own in Queen’s Domain. It took a while to figure out the basics of movement and combat as I danced around carnivorous ladybugs and hid from fish that loved nothing more than to dive out of the water in pursuit of my precious derriere, but otherwise my years of experience playing games like Dark Souls and King’s Field meant I always knew what to expect. That is, until I encountered my first mimic. Considering how many sick surprises this indie adventure loves to throw at you, I should’ve seen it coming. But when every single other chest in the opening area rewarded me with an assortment of new weapons and healing items, surely this wooden vessel atop the cliffside held similar goodies? I was a fool. The second I opened the chest, a pair of bulbous human eyes were staring back at me in ferocious anger, like I’d woken a bear from hibernation. And now, its only goal was to tear me limb from limb. Queen's Domain's mimic is the stuff of nightmares. Upon waking, a fleshy tentacle protrudes from the bottom of its chest-shaped body and two sharp claws burst from its sides, which the creature then uses to begin crawling towards you. It pursues you with an instinctual urge to destroy that nothing else in the game has had up until this point. I can handle small insects and the occasional skeleton with ease, but this thing? It needs Jesus. I managed to outsmart it by running up a nearby staircase and jumping straight back down, creating enough distance between that horrific creature and myself that it eventually fell off a ledge and spent the next several minutes trying to find a way back up in order to keep chasing me. That’s the most terrifying thing about this game's mimic--it never stops coming. How the mimic is presented set my imagination running wild. Perhaps the poor monstrosity stuck inside the chest used to be an adventurer just like me, only I was lucky enough to escape and fight another day while he must spend the rest of eternity in…

title: Sony Cancels Live-Service PS5 Game Fairgames, But No Layoffs
description: Sony has canceled the upcoming live-service shooter Fairgame$, but there will be no job cuts connected to the game's closure. This is according to a report from Bloomberg today. The game was in the works at Haven Studios in Montreal, a team founded by former Assassin's Creed veteran Jade Raymond. She left the studio back in 2023, and Fairgame$ was delayed to 2026 at the time. Now the game is scrapped entirely. According to the report, Haven "reworked" the Fairgame$ concept several times in the past three years. The studio was reportedly planning to re-reveal it with a new name. Going forward, Haven staff will support other PlayStation projects, the report said. You can watch the original CGI reveal trailer for Fairgame$ below. Fairgame$ was officially canceled following a playtest that didn't show strong results. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle said in a memo seen by Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” Creative director Mathieu Leduc said in a blog post that Haven was founded with the goal of making games that its staffers wanted to play, and that’s why the team chose a competitive multiplayer game. “Fairgame$ came from a desire to create a new type of PvP game with emergent sandbox gameplay. We want to deliver a fresh multiplayer experience that rewards creativity and mastery and delivers surprising stories each and every time you play,” Leduc said. “In a nutshell, this is a thrilling competitive heist game where you join an underground movement to rob the ultra-rich and rebalance the scales,” Leduc said. As you can see in the announcement trailer, Fairgame$ has players going after billionaires who have “too much money and too much power.”…

title: GTA 6 Backflips Look Good Now, But There Could Be More To The Story
description: A new Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer debuted today, November 10, and the video showed off a race car driver doing a backflip. The animation looks smoooth. That's notable because the Extended Look trailer that debuted back in August showed Jason doing a backflip and people online quickly roasted it for looking... off. Other said it looked totally fine. Whatever the case, some are saying this new backflip animation being featured in the latest trailer is an example of Rockstar taking feedback seriously, but it could be more nuanced than that. That's a nice backflip. That's because it subsequently came to light that the backflip animation in GTA 6 is controlled by the player and isn't locked to one specific animation. However, we don't know who is doing the backflip in this newest clip. If the character in the trailer is an NPC, as people on Reddit are surmising, then the animation could have been motion-captured as opposed to being player-controlled, hence why it looks less janky. In any event, this backflip stuff becoming a "controversy," if you can even call it that, is yet another example of how ramped-up people are for GTA 6. People are so jazzed for the release that they are poring over even the smallest details, which you may never even notice when playing the game for yourself. GTA 6 releases on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and preloading is live now. The game unlocks at midnight local time on November 19, and that means people in the US will be among the last in the world to play.

title: Amid Higher Gas And Grocery Prices, GTA 6 Is A “Bargain” At $80, Take-Two CEO Says
description: It's no secret that life is expensive. Gas and grocery prices are up, in particular, and against that backdrop, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick believes GTA 6 at $80 is a "bargain" due to how many hours people can play it. "I think the consumer is under pressure. these are challenging times. Inflation has hit average consumers. Food prices are up. Gas prices are way up, and it's taking a toll," he told CNBC. "I think we are going to see that as we head into the Christmas season undoubtedly. Entertainment is not immune to such forces." What gives Zelnick hope in this environment is that, in his belief, "interactive entertainment is actually a real bargain," and particularly a game like GTA. "There are so many hours of engagement on offer. Even a short video game is 10 hours of engagement on the low end. You can play Grand Theft Auto 5 for hundreds of hours and not get bored. We'll see how people feel about Grand Theft Auto 6, but I believe that you'll be able to engage for an extraordinary long period of time," he said. "So if consumers look at entertainment value as the intersection of how great it is and how long you can engage with it, interactive entertainment is a great bargain. However, when you give people what they want, no matter what the times are, they will show up for it." GTA 6's base edition costs $80, while there is also a $100 Ultimate Edition featuring a variety of additional in-game content. GTA 5, meanwhile, launched at $60 in 2013; that same $60 is about $85 today after adjusting for inflation. This is a point that Zelnick has made repeatedly when explaining why GTA 6 is actually a very good value. He's also said Rockstar could have charged even more for GTA 6, but chose not to so the game could reach more people. While GTA 6's price is actually lower than what GTA 5 launched at in 2013, the same cannot be said for the hardware people need to play it on. title: Valve Is Giving You More Ways To Know If A Game Runs Well On Steam Deck
description: Valve's Steam Deck verification program has been a helpful, if somewhat flawed, method of determining if a game is a good fit for the company's handheld PC. But while many games might be granted a "Verified" badge, there have been many cases where real-world performance doesn't live up to the expectation of players. That's why Valve has introduced a more nuanced way for you to determine if a game is a good fit for the Steam Deck. Along with the Steam Deck verification status, games will now feature average frame-rate data on the store page once Valve has gathered enough data from players. This will give you an indication of real-world performance on the Steam Deck, collecting data from other players using the Steam Deck in their default states and averaging it across their total playtime. "The current Steam Deck Verified compatibility rating is based on standardized test criteria, but it may not match every customer’s bar for acceptable gameplay," the announcement post reads. "This is especially true around performance - a game with an Unsupported rating due to unstable performance may be considered playable by some customers, and a Verified game may not reach a framerate that some customers prefer to play at." Alongside the average, Valve is also adding a histogram that let's you see numerous averages spread out over playtime. This can help you determine if a game has pockets of poor performance that might be dragging down the average, giving you even more information to help you determine if a purchase for Steam Deck play is worthwhile. Valve relies on other players for this data. So while it says that thousands of games already have this featured on their store pages, there are still many more that require more playtime before they can be calculated and displayed. The data collection is opt-in, too, meaning only Steam users actively sharing their data through the Steam Beta Client will count towards these averages. Valve says it will be rolling out this program…

title: WoW: Forever Just Received Its First Big Post-Launch Changes
description: World of Warcraft: Forever received its first post-launch updates over the weekend, giving players a good reason to run each dungeon more than once alongside upcoming class tweaks. On November 8, developer Blizzard issued a hotfix that increased kill experience while in dungeons by 50%. According to the forum post, Blizzard said this is so it "feels better to go back for more runs," and made reference to a Wailing Caverns dungeon quest to collect Deviate Hides that often requires more than one run. It previously outlined upcoming class changes that will go live on November 10. Those changes will make it so Hunter and Warlock pets are sturdier, improve Affliction Warlock's damage-over-time spells, and make it so Enhancement Shamans will want to pursue strength and attack power items instead of intellect and spell power ones. The debate on how much experience dungeons should grant in Forever has been an ongoing back and forth since the game's beta. Initially, dungeons were particularly lucrative, with massive experience rewards from dungeon quests. That changed about halfway through the beta due to concerns that players were leveling too quickly while doing dungeons. Blizzard axed dungeon quest experience as a result. While dungeons were still worthwhile to do once thanks to potent item rewards, doing them multiple times proved to be less valuable. With no quests to do, kill experience earned in dungeons was lackluster. Forever's launch on November 4 carried that philosophy forward, but it quickly became apparent dungeons were simply not worth doing after one quest-focused run. It was even more of an issue considering that many dungeons have item-collection quests that are difficult to complete in a single run when all five members of the group are trying to do it at once. However, because doing a dungeon a second time was so inefficient when it came to earning experience, going back in to try and complete that quest felt like a waste of time. In an episode of the…
